billing_free_desc: Free supports individual local use; external providers may have their own fees and limits. Pro adds hosted capabilities that depend on Vectora Services, such as organizations, invitations, remote webhooks, and Connect.

capabilities_subtitle: Every capability below is shared between you and the agent. Plans, decisions, and runs are recorded — nothing hidden behind a tool call.
capability_browser_desc: A workbench connected to the Chromium distributed with Electron. User and agent share pages and context; sessions, cookies, and new tabs depend on the sidecar and UI integration.
capability_context_graph_desc: A typed code graph across ~30 languages (tree-sitter), impact analysis, and GraphRAG — the same source of truth the agent's tool and your UI both query.
capability_explorer_desc: Optimistic conflict resolution when you and the agent edit the same file, full-text search shared with the agent's own tool, and per-commit file history.
capability_git_desc: Isolated worktrees, stash, diff/merge in an overlay, and PR creation without leaving the app.
capability_sandbox_desc: Native isolation on Linux with bubblewrap, seccomp, and Landlock. Windows requires WSL2 with bwrap. Without effective isolation, the worker has no filesystem or network isolation; HITL exemptions require an active sandbox.
capability_terminal_desc: A persistent PTY session — survives navigation and remounts, the same shell seen live by you and the agent, inside the sandbox, when active.

downloads_install_linux: AppImage: chmod +x Vectora-*.AppImage && ./Vectora-*.AppImage. Packages are also available for Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora/RHEL, Arch, Snap, and Flatpak.
downloads_install_macos: Drag Vectora.app into the Applications folder. If Gatekeeper blocks it from opening, run xattr -cr /Applications/Vectora.app once in Terminal.
downloads_install_windows: Run the .exe and follow the installer. If Windows SmartScreen warns you, click "More info" → "Run anyway" (common for new apps until the certificate builds reputation). Prefer silent install? Use Vectora-Setup.exe /S. The .msi integrates with Apps & Features — useful for IT-managed rollouts.

faq_geral_1_answer: Vectora is a self-hosted AI agent. The Free entitlement supports individual local use, including the web interface; the Pro entitlement unlocks team features and selected connected services. The instance runs on your own computer or server.
faq_geral_2_answer: Install Vectora on Windows, macOS, or Linux; Docker is only needed for optional external services such as complete storage. You can run Vectora locally or on your own VPS without Pro. Pro is only required for team features and hosted services that depend on Services.
faq_geral_3_answer: No. Vectora uses LLMs and embeddings via API (Google, Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, Voyage, OpenRouter) or local Ollama. For individual use, any recent laptop runs it fine; for a team VPS, 2 vCPUs and 4 GB RAM are already enough.
faq_geral_3_question: Do I need a GPU to run it?
faq_instalacao_1_answer: Windows 10+, macOS 12+, and Linux (Ubuntu 20.04+/Debian 11+/Fedora 35+) — native installers for all three, with built-in auto-update.
faq_instalacao_2_answer: You can self-host Vectora on a Linux VPS without Pro. Pro is reserved for hosted capabilities that depend on Services, such as organizations and invitations, remote webhooks, and Connect.
faq_instalacao_2_question: How do I deploy on a server for my team?
faq_instalacao_3_answer: A local individual installation does not require an account. Download the installer for your system and start the app. An account is only needed for features or connected services that require one; complete storage also needs Postgres, Qdrant, and Redis.
faq_planos_1_answer: Free lets an individual use the CLI and Desktop locally. Local capabilities such as RAG, installed Library content, Browser, Sandbox, Context Graph, HITL, Decision Models, self-hosting, and PostgreSQL, Qdrant, or Redis storage remain available. Pro enables hosted capabilities that depend on Services, including organizations, remote webhooks, and Connect. External providers may charge separately.
faq_planos_1_question: What's the difference between Free and Pro?
faq_planos_2_answer: No, not for individual local use. The Free entitlement works without signing in. An account is required for Pro features and connected services that require sign-in or an active entitlement.
faq_planos_2_question: Do I need to create an account to use Vectora?
faq_planos_3_answer: Yes. No minimum commitment. Cancel from the dashboard anytime — your account automatically reverts to the Free entitlement.
faq_seguranca_1_answer: No. Everything stays on your server. Vectora has no access to your documents, conversations, or code.
faq_seguranca_1_question: Is my data sent to Vectora?
faq_seguranca_2_answer: Yes. Since your data stays on your own infrastructure, you keep full control over compliance.
faq_seguranca_2_question: Is Vectora LGPD and GDPR compliant?
faq_seguranca_3_answer: On Free, it's local use with no login. For Pro (account required), Vectora's own authentication supports email/password and magic links.
faq_tecnico_1_answer: Google Gemini (default), Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, Ollama (local), OpenRouter (proxy with hundreds of models), and any OpenAI-API-compatible provider.
faq_tecnico_2_answer: Embeddings via Cohere, Voyage, Ollama, or OpenRouter (local or hosted), LanceDB as the default vector store with dense vector search and optional reranking (Cohere/Voyage). In Complete mode (self-hosted with Postgres + Qdrant), search becomes hybrid (dense + BM25).
faq_tecnico_3_answer: No. Vectora is a workspace with AI — you and the agent share the filesystem, terminal, git, and browser inside the product itself, with no public REST API or embedded MCP server.
faq_tecnico_3_question: Does Vectora expose a public API or MCP server?
features_agent_run_desc: Track executions by run_id, lifecycle state, parent/subagent relationships, and linked evidence. The event ledger supports history reconstruction. Local installs use SQLite; distributed deployments can configure PostgreSQL. Resuming depends on available checkpoints and storage.
features_agent_run_summary: Runs with persistent identity, state, and evidence.
features_browser_desc: Browser Workbench navigation uses Electron Chromium when its sidecar and workspace session are available. Destination controls apply to fetch, crawl and map. Search sends queries to the selected provider without applying the egress policy. fetch_url can use Chromium as a fallback; web_crawl and web_map require TAVILY_API_KEY and have no Chromium fallback.
features_connect_desc: Vectora bots available on several messaging platforms — Telegram is the first, with more to come — so you can talk to your agent without opening the app. Each bot is activated from the Vectora Pro panel; Vectora Services acts as the relay, providing the fixed URL each platform requires.
features_connect_summary: Talk to Vectora through Telegram and other chat platforms.
features_context_graph_desc: Combines structural parsing via tree-sitter with semantic extraction by an LLM to build a real graph of your repository's symbols, imports, and calls — not a generic text index. Powers GraphRAG search (relevance by graph proximity, not just vector similarity) and impact analysis: before applying a change, the agent can ask "what else does this affect?" and get an answer grounded in the code's actual structure, not a guess.
features_decision_models_desc: Clef, Laya, JEV, and compatible providers evaluate structured decisions. In Settings → AI Models, choose a provider and enable the surfaces that may consult it; in chat, choose when to use the model. Decisions do not grant permissions: policy, gates, and local controls prevail. An unavailable provider is not an approval.
features_decision_models_summary: Structured evaluations configurable per runtime surface.
features_desktop_desc: The desktop application is distributed under the AGPL-3.0 license, with an Electron interface and a Python backend compiled via Nuitka. In desktop mode, the two layers communicate over a local named pipe or Unix socket, without opening a TCP port on your machine.
features_desktop_summary: Windows x64/ARM64, macOS Apple Silicon, and Linux x64/ARM64 — Electron + compiled backend.
features_egress_policies_desc: The workspace egress policy defines allowed and denied hosts, ports, and private-IP blocking, and validates the destination after DNS resolution. It applies to the URL-based web tools (fetch, crawl, map) and to Browser Workbench navigation. Network isolation for commands depends on the sandbox backend: lockdown denies network access when the worker runs under bwrap, and allow_tcp_ports requires Landlock ABI V4 (kernel 6.7+) on Linux. In the Chromium fallback of fetch_url, only the initial URL is checked: redirects are not revalidated and the destination IP is not pinned.
features_egress_policies_summary: Hosts, ports, and private IPs controlled per workspace.
features_explorer_desc: A workspace file tree with inline editing, create/rename/delete, and direct integration with the agent's context — drag a file into the chat, or ask the agent to open and edit something, and both views (yours and its) stay in sync in real time.
features_git_desc: A full Git panel in the workbench: visual diffs, a browsable commit history, stash, worktrees, and branch comparison — no need to leave the chat and open a terminal just to run `git log`. The agent sees the same repository state you see on screen.
features_i18n_desc: The entire interface — chat, settings, onboarding — is translated into 7 languages: Portuguese, English, Spanish, French, Italian, German, and Russian. No hardcoded strings: every visible piece of text goes through a central message system, so adding a new language doesn't require hunting for strings scattered across the code.
features_i18n_summary: Full interface in Portuguese, English, Spanish, and 4 more languages.
features_kanban_desc: A real Kanban board on top of the agent engine: create tasks, assign them to an agent profile, define dependencies between them (with cycle detection), and track progress live via SSE. Every background run has a heartbeat watchdog that proves the agent is still alive — if it stops beating, the task is released back to the queue instead of getting stuck forever. Optional review column, subtask progress rollup, and multiple boards per workspace.
features_kanban_summary: Delegate background tasks with dependencies, priority, and review.
features_library_desc: Use installed skills and content locally for free. Browsing catalogs, publishing packages, and downloading Library content is also free with your account login. Every item shows clear provenance (official, verified, or community) — nothing gets installed blind.
features_library_summary: Publish, search, and reuse curated skills, connectors, and memories.
features_mcp_desc: Vectora consumes external MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers as a client. Connecting your own server and using installed connectors are local capabilities; browsing hosted catalogs requires Pro. Deliberately, Vectora never exposes itself as an MCP server: that would make RAG and its other tools reachable from outside the shared workspace, which is the product's real differentiator.
features_mcp_summary: Connect third-party MCP servers — Vectora never becomes a server.
features_native_engine_desc: Vectora's agent runs on a conversation engine built from scratch — an imperative loop that re-reads the session history on every turn, streams the model call, and executes tool calls, without relying on a compiled node graph or an external orchestration framework. Conversation state never lives only in memory: it's always re-read from persistent storage, so a session survives a backend restart without losing context.
features_native_engine_summary: A purpose-built imperative loop, no external orchestration framework.
features_native_media_desc: Any attached file reaches the model in a form it understands. PDFs, videos, and audio are sent natively when the model accepts them; when the model only reads images, a PDF becomes pages and a video becomes frames (limits and resolution are configurable, and the pdf_to_images and video_to_frames tools accept other values); when it reads neither, the extracted text or the transcript is sent instead. Screenshots and images from tools, including MCP tools, reach the model as images, and audio returned by MCP tools is transcribed locally. Embedded ffmpeg/ffprobe analyze audio and video on this computer, and transcription runs here (embedded faster-whisper, native macOS speech recognition, or the system whisper) without sending anything to a provider. YouTube videos (and any platform supported by yt-dlp) are read first via the public transcript — without downloading the whole video — with on-demand frame extraction only when the agent needs visual context for a specific moment.
features_native_media_summary: PDFs, images, audio, and video reach the model in the format it accepts, with local transcription.
features_nine_router_desc: 9Router is an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible proxy that reuses the OAuth login of subscriptions you already pay for — OpenAI Codex, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, and more — exposing all of them behind a single endpoint. Point Vectora at that proxy's URL and key in settings, and those subscriptions' models show up right in the chat, with no separate per-token charge. It's the opposite of OpenRouter (aggregated catalog, pay-per-token): 9Router is about reusing what you already pay for elsewhere.
features_nine_router_summary: Use your Codex, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot, and other subscriptions right inside Vectora, no per-token billing.
features_ollama_desc: Vectora detects an Ollama instance running on your machine and registers the available models directly into the chat's model picker — no config file to edit, no app restart. Run a fully offline local model, with zero API cost, through the same flow you'd use a hosted model.
features_ollama_summary: Local models show up in chat automatically, no manual setup.
features_openrouter_desc: Connect your OpenRouter key and get access to their entire aggregated model catalog — from dozens of different providers, in one place — without needing a separate account for each. You pay the provider directly, with no Vectora markup.
features_openrouter_summary: A catalog with hundreds of models, using your own API key.
features_plan_mode_desc: Plan Mode turns plans into executable steps with dependencies and gates before actions requiring approval. Kanban organizes tasks and background delegations. Permissions, checkpoints, and storage determine what can resume after interruption.
features_plan_mode_summary: Steps, dependencies, background execution, and approval gates.
features_rag_desc: Embeddings via Cohere, Voyage, Ollama (local), or OpenRouter, indexed in LanceDB. In Complete mode, search combines dense (vector) retrieval with BM25 (lexical) — covering both "find something similar to this" and "find the file that has exactly this word". An optional reranker reorders results before they reach the agent's context, prioritizing precision over raw recall.
features_rag_summary: Embeddings from multiple providers, vector indexing, and optional reranking.
features_sandbox_desc: Native isolation on Linux with bubblewrap, seccomp, and Landlock. Windows requires WSL2 with bwrap. Without effective isolation, the worker has no filesystem or network isolation; HITL exemptions require an active sandbox.
features_sandbox_summary: Filesystem and network isolation for workers, native on Linux; Windows and macOS have their own requirements.
features_services_desc: Vectora Services provides the update server, account login and token, subscription checkout and management, and account data export and deletion for Free users. Hosted product capabilities — including organizations, Connect, and remote webhooks — require Pro.
features_services_summary: The Cloudflare Worker that powers the infrastructure behind Vectora.
features_souls_desc: The orchestrator dynamically delegates to one of 10 SOULs depending on the task: Coder (files/terminal/git), Search (web/RAG), Reviewer (reads diffs, never writes), Tester, DevOps (CI/infra), Writer/Docs, Data Analyst, Security Auditor, Browser QA, and Planner. The tool restriction per SOUL is real enforcement — a bind on the model's function-calling, not a prompt suggestion: a SOUL without write access can't change a file, no matter how insistently the request asks. All of them share the same native conversation engine and the same tool registry — behavior profiles on the same foundation, not separate products.
features_souls_summary: A catalog of specialized subagents — code, research, review, testing, DevOps, and more —, all running on the same native engine.
features_storage_avancado_desc: Configure PostgreSQL, Qdrant, and Redis as alternatives to embedded storage. They run on the operator's chosen infrastructure and do not require a Pro subscription.
features_storage_avancado_summary: PostgreSQL, Qdrant and Redis instead of the default embedded storage.
features_terminal_desc: A real terminal inside the workbench, not a text box pretending to be one — commands actually run, with output streaming, multiple tabs per workspace, and persistent per-session history. The agent and the user share the same terminal: what one runs, the other sees.
features_verification_lab_desc: Per-workspace quality-gate profiles distinguish approval, failure, blocking, degradation, and unverified results. Evaluation Lab replays cassettes with known credentials hidden and compares runs with vectora eval run and vectora eval compare, without external calls. Replay and live validations marked as skipped do not prove live provider or integration availability. Only known credential fields and patterns are hidden; messages and responses can retain private code or personal data. Restrict access and review cassettes before sharing.
features_verification_lab_summary: Quality gates, run evidence, cassettes, and replay.
features_vps_desc: Run Vectora on your own server. The instance stays available while your personal computer is off; availability and resources depend on your infrastructure and configuration.
features_vps_summary: Run Vectora on your own server instead of only on your computer.
features_web_multiuser_desc: The web interface can be used locally by one person. An active Pro entitlement is required to invite additional members and operate a shared instance with roles and permissions.
features_web_multiuser_summary: The same Vectora, hosted, with accounts and role-based permissions.
